title: The parts every entry of the registry of the game's code is made of
description: Shared by the function, type and global entries of registry and by the live layer in the home. registry/README.md is the rule.

id.description: A registry id: the name as the game writes it, scope by ::, a member after a dot, a compiler's piece after @ (registry/README.md).

rung.description: How certain a name or a type is, strongest first. Applied (the decompiler may be given it as a real name or type): game - the game's own name (macOS symbols, FieldMeta); toolkit - the Toolkit's exported name; confirmed - ours, with the evidence of an instrument (a watch, a read) or a test. Shown (a comment beside the code, never in it): inferred - reasoning from the code or a pairing; extender - Script Extender's author's name, unchecked; guess - supposed, with what it rests on and what would confirm it; unknown - nothing backs it.

knownAs.description: The names other sources give the same thing, so that a reader who comes with one finds the entry.

source.description: extender: Script Extender's declaration; extender-legacy: the earlier name Script Extender keeps as an alias in Lua (bg3::legacy); toolkit: the Toolkit's export; symbols: the symbol database's match; decompiler: the decompiler's default name; macos: the macOS build's symbol.

state.description: How far the reading has got: described - the entry says what the thing is; looked_at - looked at and not understood; unlooked - never looked at (an entry made only to be cited, a callee).

guess.description: A supposition, written as a statement about the code: what it rests on and what would confirm it.

questions.description: What is open about an entry, written so that someone who knows the game, a modder or another agent can read the entry alone and help: above all how the thing is reached from the game - what a player or a test would do for this code to run or this field to change.

ask.description: The question, about the code and the game.

about.description: reach: how the game makes the code run or the field change; conditions: what decides its path; meaning: what a value stands for.

tried.description: What was tried and what it showed.

source.description: Where the answer comes from: a test's address, a wiki page, an instrument's reading.

comments.description: Our comments at a place of the entry: an instruction's offset from the function's start (+0x2B), a field's offset, a member's name.

concept.description: The game's own concept the entry belongs to.

name.description: The concept's name where it is not the entry itself: a system's, a rule's (by its wiki page or stats name).

ext_name.description: The name Script Extender's Lua answers to.

storage.description: Where a parameter or local lives: reg:rcx, reg:xmm1, stack:+0x28 (from the stack pointer at entry), stack:-0x24C; unresolved where only the decompiler's temporary name is known so far.

type.description: The type as C++ writes it.

type_id.description: The type's registry id, where it has one.

decompiler_name.description: Only with storage unresolved: the decompiler's temporary name it was given under, until its storage is read.
